messages:
mia_support: heads-up — customer acme-prod hit a big wave of 429s this morning when calling rwd-large-ctx64. They say most requests include ~60k tokens in the prompt (multi-file concat) + streaming completion. Example response header from their logs:

  HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
  Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2026 10:15:08 GMT
  x-rwd-reason: per_model_tpm_exceeded
  x-rwd-model: rwd-large-ctx64
  content-type: application/json
  
  Body: {"error":"rate_limit", "message":"per-model TPM exceeded"}

  They also included this minimal repro curl (sanitized API key):
  ```bash
  curl -i -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \n    -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \n    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n    -d '{"model":"rwd-large-ctx64","prompt":"<~60k tokens>\", "max_tokens":256}'
  ```

  Question: can someone confirm the per-model RPM/TPM and max_concurrency for this variant? Also: do very long prompts (>=32k) get an additional throttling policy (e.g., lower concurrency or separate bucket)? Customer is asking why short prompts are fine but these long requests spike 429s.

samir_eng: quick notes — long contexts absolutely change the accounting. TPM counts prompt+completion tokens, so a 60k prompt eats a ton of the TPM budget per request. For rwd-large-ctx64 the practical per-model TPM ceiling we enforce at the edge is lower for sustained traffic because of fairness buckets; short bursts might succeed but sustained fanout causes per-model exhaustion. I don't want to call out a public exact number in thread, but for debugging you can check the model profile in the console (Console -> Models -> rwd-large-ctx64 -> Limits).

priya_platform: adding to samir — we do have an internal heuristic where requests with context > 32k are routed to a throttled path: reduced concurrency and stronger per-minute accounting to avoid OOMs on certain backends. That routing is transparent to users (they still hit same endpoint) which explains why short prompts succeed while big ones get 429s under similar QPS.

priya_platform: repro suggestion: run a tight loop of non-streaming requests with identical payloads and vary prompt size (8k, 24k, 40k, 60k). You should see the failure rate jump around the 32k-48k region. Example test harness (very small, non-prod):
  ```bash
  for size in 8000 24000 40000 60000; do
    echo "== size=$size ==";
    python -c "import requests,os,json; p='x'*$size; r=requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', headers={'Authorization':'Bearer REDACTED'}, json={'model':'rwd-large-ctx64','prompt':p,'max_tokens':16}); print(r.status_code, r.text[:200])"
  done
  ```

jeremy_sre: also check customer-level quotas and burst windows — sometimes a single customer hits global per-model TPM but still has per-api-key burst capacity which gets used up. Recommend enabling exponential backoff with full jitter on their client and add an immediate fallback to a shorter-context model (rwd-large-ctx32 or a streaming-only fallback) for large inputs. Can someone from support capture their exact X-Request-Id headers for a few failed requests? I want to correlate with edge logs.

mia_support: got two failed request ids from customer: rq_3f8a1b and rq_3f8a4c (both 429s at ~10:15:08). forwarding now. :pray:

deploy-bot: deployment note — rolled out model throttle tweak (opt-in) to regions eu-west-1 and us-west-2 at 2026-03-16T09:40Z. See #eng-runtime for rollout details. :gear:

samir_eng: TL;DR: long-context = more TPM consumption + routed to stricter throttle path. Fixes: reduce per-request prompt size, shard fanout (stagger requests), or use smaller-context variant. We'll help repro and consider whether to grant a temporary per-customer bump for acme-prod while they re-architect.

priya_platform: I'll open a private ticket to evaluate a short-term increase for their committed Dedicated plan or add a canary policy. tagging @jeremy_sre to correlate logs.

mia_support: thanks — I'll collect more X-Request-Id samples and coordinate with customer about fallbacks. :thumbsup:
